Let agents work.Keep the keys.

01

Your accounts stay in a vault

Agents use GitHub or Gmail through Anchi. They never see the password or the token.

the agent asks→with a fake key→the gatekeeper swaps in the real one→GitHub · Gmail · AWS
02

Every task runs in its own sealed cell

It cannot read your files unless you share a folder with it, and it uses only the accounts you switch on for it.

a new task→a fresh sealed cell→reads only shared folders→credential scan before it closes
03

Risky actions wait for you

Sending, posting and merging ask first. Approve or deny in one click from the Needs you inbox; a write left waiting is refused when its time runs out.

send · post · merge→Needs you→you approve→it runs·refused on timeout
[i]

The vault keeps your keys at home. What an agent reads still reaches the model behind its AI account. Security model ↗

Three steps to your first agent.Nothing here needs a terminal.

  1. 1

    Set up the secure room

    Anchi installs the sealed space your agents run in, the vault and the gatekeeper on this computer. It asks once before it installs anything; the first time takes several minutes.

  2. 2

    Sign in to an AI account

    ChatGPT, Claude or another provider, in your browser. One is enough.

  3. 3

    Meet your first agent

    Pick a ready-made agent and give it a first task. No folder or account is shared until you say so.

Later agents start from a description or a template under New agent; before one exists, Anchi says in plain words which accounts it acts through, which folders it reads and which teammates it can hand work to. Desktop guide ↗

Runs on your computer,with your own AI account.

$ curl -fsSL https://anchi.elseward.xyz/install.sh | sh -s -- --desktop

One line installs the desktop app and its command-line tools, checked against the release's SHA-256. Then open Anchi; the three steps run inside it. Setup guide ↗

Before you start.What to expect.

Documentation · Release notes · Report a problem · Report a vulnerability privately

Which AI account do I need?

One of ChatGPT, Claude or another OpenAI-compatible provider. You sign in from the app, in your browser, with no CLI to install. Agents think with that account and use its subscription quota or API credit. A starter agent can be made without any model call. First-task guide ↗

What does setup need?

On an Apple Silicon Mac, Anchi downloads what the secure room needs and checks it, so there is nothing to install first. Linux needs QEMU and KVM. The secure room takes half of your computer's CPUs and memory by default, which you can change, and at least 8 GB of disk plus room for your projects. The first setup takes several minutes.

Does everything stay on my computer?

Your passwords and tokens do: they stay in the vault and never enter a cell. What an agent reads can reach the model behind its AI account and the websites it may visit. By default that is any public website. Under Advanced you can limit it to a list; the services it is connected to stay reachable, and Firecrawl, when connected, can fetch pages outside the list.

Is this ready for my real accounts?

Release packages are not signed yet. If that matters to you, build and run Anchi from source, the desktop app included (scripts/anchi-desktop), so what runs is code you can review. Anchi has not completed a third-party security audit; before connecting sensitive production accounts, try the access and approval flow with test accounts.

Prefer a terminal?

The same team also runs in the TUI and the CLI, with the same vault, cells and approvals. After you update the app, Needs you tells you when the secure room needs an update too. TUI keys ↗
